comparison: Three fresh baseline and three fresh author-definition-refined Pseudo-seq trials; identical reviewer instructions
interpretation: Exploratory within-paper comparison; n=3 per arm. Chosen after a known error. Does not estimate general accuracy or establish causal model reasoning; no paired random seed is available.

source_plan.reason_for_fresh_extraction: User explicitly requests three fresh Pseudo-seq runs with the current definition and three with a refined information_effect definition to investigate the documented local-condition error. Same sources; do not reuse completed authors. This is a controlled development experiment, not re-curation.
source_plan.interpretation: Targeted diagnostic repeat after a documented general instruction correction. Compare with archived baseline and run_01; one sample per condition, no blinded expert evaluation or general accuracy estimate.

evaluation_not_given_to_models.primary: For each first author, source-check every information_effect and its agreement with local States, mechanism, description and typed effects; count runs with at least one unsupported or condition-inappropriate claim.
error_categories: wrong information carrier or physical form
direct signal confused with downstream inference
contradiction with connected States or other Operation fields
secondary: number and nature of affected Operations
review detection, missed issues and false-positive requests
exact correction fields and final residual errors
elapsed time and native reported token usage
scoring_rules: Shared statements are valid if true for all declared conditions; identical wording alone is not an error.
Do not require particular labels, node counts or separate treatment nodes if condition correspondence remains explicit.
Missing optional information is not automatically an error.
Review acceptance is an outcome, not independent ground truth.
Do not alter the contract, sources or max-revisions mid-experiment; retain failures.
Assess treatment-specific claim, mock background stops and comparative inference separately.
